title: Review a mutation flow with no rollback after optimistic update
description: Problem: Review a mutation flow with no rollback after optimistic update. Solve this problem with multiple approaches and detailed explanations.

data.text: **Review a mutation flow with no rollback after optimistic update** exposes a silent data-integrity bug. Optimistic updates make the UI feel instant by assuming the mutation will succeed, but when the server rejects the change, the cache must revert to the previous state. Without a rollback, the user sees data that does not match the server, leading to confusion, duplicate actions, and corrupt local state.
What a broken flow looks like

items: The user marks a todo as complete, the UI updates immediately, but the API returns 500
The todo stays checked in the UI even though the server never confirmed it
A second mutation fires on top of the incorrect optimistic state
The user refreshes the page and sees the todo is still incomplete, eroding trust
Subsequent queries overwrite the optimistic state with stale server data
The error is swallowed silently because the onError handler is missing

terms.definition: A UI change applied before the server confirms it, assuming the mutation will succeed.
Restoring the previous state when an optimistic update fails, using a snapshot taken before mutation.
A deep copy of the pre-mutation state saved so it can be restored on failure.
Refetching or updating the query cache after a mutation to reconcile client and server state.
A unique token sent with a mutation so the server can deduplicate retries and prevent duplicate creates.

data.title: Phases of a resilient mutation
items: **Snapshot**: save the current cache or state before touching it
**Optimistic apply**: update the UI immediately with the expected change
**Server mutation**: fire the actual API call in the background
**Success**: replace the optimistic state with the server-confirmed data
**Rollback**: restore the snapshot if the server rejects, and surface the error to the user

data.caption: Optimistic mutation lifecycle with rollback
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[User action] --> B[onMutate: snapshot cache]
    B --> C[Apply optimistic change]
    C --> D[Render updated UI]
    D --> E[Fire mutation to server]
    E --> F{Server responds?}
    F -->|Success| G[onSettled: invalidate / refetch]
    F -->|Error| H[onError: restore snapshot]
    H --> I[Show error to user]
    G --> J[UI reflects confirmed state]
    I --> K[User can retry]
    K --> E

data.title: Cancel before you mutate
data.text: Always cancel in-flight queries at the start of onMutate. If a refetch is already running, it will complete after your optimistic update and overwrite it with stale data.

items: Double-click: disable the trigger with isPending to prevent duplicate mutations
Out-of-order response: mutation B finishes before A, corrupting state. Use sequential mutations or cancel in-flight ones
Partial failure: one item in a batch fails. Decide whether to roll back the whole batch or keep successful updates
Stale snapshot: if another component modified the same query between onMutate and onError, restoring the snapshot may undo unrelated changes
Concurrent users: if another user edits the same item, the server may return a conflict. Surface a merge UI rather than silently overwriting

cards.title: Optimistic with rollback
cards.description: Update UI immediately, restore on error.
pros: Great UX when success rate is high

cards.title: Pessimistic
cards.description: Wait for server response before updating UI.

cards.title: Background refetch
cards.description: Keep optimistic UI but always refetch and reconcile after.
cons: May flash updated data back to old state

data.title: Add rollback to a broken mutation
data.description: Find a mutation in your project that updates the cache optimistically but lacks an onError handler. Add snapshot capture and rollback logic. Verify by forcing the API to return 500 and confirming the UI reverts.
steps: Locate a useMutation that calls setQueryData before the server responds
Add onMutate: cancel queries, snapshot the current data, apply the optimistic change
Add onError: restore the snapshot and surface an error message
Add onSettled: invalidate the query to refetch confirmed data
Test by mocking the API to fail and observing the rollback
data.expectedOutcome: The UI should revert to the pre-mutation state on failure, and the user should see an explicit error message.

items.question: When should I avoid optimistic updates?
items.answer: When the failure rate is high (payments, irreversible deletes), when the user needs server-side validation before the change applies, or when rollback logic would be more complex than the feature itself.

items.question: How does this differ with Server Actions?
items.answer: Next.js Server Actions integrate with useOptimistic from React, which handles snapshot and rollback automatically. You still need to handle isPending and error states for a complete experience.

items.question: What if the optimistic state is in Redux, not React Query?
items.answer: Use Redux Undo or manually store the previous state in the action payload. The pattern is identical: snapshot, apply, commit or revert. Redux requires more boilerplate because there is no built-in mutation lifecycle.

data.title: Summary
points: Optimistic updates require an explicit rollback path
Snapshot the cache before mutating so you can restore it on error
Cancel in-flight queries before applying optimistic changes
Disable triggers during isPending to prevent double mutations
Surface errors to the user; silent rollback erodes trust
data.takeaway: A mutation without rollback is not optimistic—it is just guessing.
